_comment_1: AUDIT SESSION SETTINGS (#221 RoE 1) — THE FALLBACK ROUTE. Launch with:  claude --settings .claude/settings.audit.json
_comment_0: NOT THE NORMAL ROUTE ANY MORE (ruled 2026-08-08). The audit lane is C:\grok_build\RD_Audit, a dedicated directory whose own .claude/settings.local.json layers by default and whose own CLAUDE.md IS the auditor's orientation — no flag, and none of the work lanes give up their CLAUDE.md. This file is what remains for auditing FROM a work lane, and it has one gap the lane does not: it excludes CLAUDE.md without putting anything in its place, so a session launched this way must open Blueprint/AUDITOR_ORIENTATION.md by hand before it reads any source.
_comment_2: Excludes the two ALWAYS-ON priming sources so an audit slice is not handed prior conclusions about the subsystem it is auditing.
_comment_3: This layers ON TOP of .claude/settings.json, so the project permissions and the PostToolUse/SessionStart hooks still apply. Do not copy them here.
_comment_claudeMd: CLAUDE.md is loaded into every agent's context on every turn and is dense with per-subsystem conclusions, gate-score narratives and standing traps. Globs are matched against ABSOLUTE paths. Both slash directions are listed for every entry because the repo lives on Windows (C:\grok_build\...) and picomatch is forward-slash oriented, and a silently-unmatched pattern looks exactly like a clean audit.
_comment_nowildcards: THE LIST IS EXPLICIT AND CARRIES NO WILDCARDS, and tools/audit_preflight.js check 3b enforces that. Until 2026-08-08 a `**/grok_build/**/CLAUDE.md` catch-all headed it as belt-and-braces. Once the audit lane moved to C:\grok_build\RD_Audit that pattern became a defect: it also matches RD_Audit/CLAUDE.md, the AUDITOR'S OWN orientation document and the one file that must load. Covering a newly-added worktree is preflight check 3's job — it enumerates `git worktree list` and demands both slash forms verbatim — not a glob's.
_comment_memory: The auto-memory index loads alongside CLAUDE.md and is the worked case #221 RoE 1 actually cites: on 2026-08-02 the trip-block-hybrid-model memory described the PWR trip-block model as settled and owner-confirmed — a prior conclusion about the exact mechanism slice 1 was auditing, priming in the 'this is deliberate, do not look' direction. Excluding CLAUDE.md alone leaves this in place, which is why a straight file-swap does not solve the problem.
_comment_verify: VERIFY, DO NOT ASSUME. These take effect at session start, so they cannot be proven from inside the session that writes them. First thing in an audit session, confirm the exclusion actually happened — ask the agent whether it can see CLAUDE.md's 'Recent themes' section or the memory index. If it can, the patterns did not match and the slice is NOT independent; fix the glob before auditing, and say so in the slice issue.
